Last Friday (the 21st), during the sentencing of the Hong Kong Alliance case, a woman waiting to attend the hearing as an audience member was taken away by police in a police car in the early hours of the morning. In response to enquiries, the police stated that the woman was arrested on three charges: "behaving in a disorderly manner in a public place", "resisting or intentionally obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty", and "with seditious intent".

In the early hours of last Friday, more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts to attend the hearing. During the wait, a plainclothes police officer pointed to a woman in the queue and said he "suspected her clothing had seditious intent", and immediately took her into a police car and left. While taking the woman away, several police officers repeatedly told reporters to leave, saying they would "take them to the press area", while pulling an orange cordon line towards Yi Wa Street. The cordon was not retracted until after the woman had boarded the police car. A "court observation volunteer" who was queuing near the woman that day said she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese characters printed on it.

The Collective spoke to the police to ask about the reason the woman was taken away and whether she had been arrested. The police replied this morning (the 24th) that during a security operation around the West Kowloon Court area on the 21st of August, a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "behaving in a disorderly manner in a public place", "resisting or intentionally obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty", and "with seditious intent", and was detained for investigation.
